7,337 likes, 170 comments - unicef on October 22, 2026: "Statement by Regional Director for @unicef_mena, Edouard Beigbeder, on the ongoing killings of children across the Gaza Strip:

“Fourteen-year-old Mohamed was walking home from a UNICEF-supported learning centre on 17 October in Deir al Balah in the Gaza Strip when he was reported hit in the street by an armed drone strike and killed. His school bag was left lying beside his body.

The next day, six-year-old Misk – a first-grade student at a UNICEF learning centre - was at home when she was reported killed by gunfire in al-Maghazi. Later that day, 12-year-old Tamer was reported shot while on the ruins of his home in the Beit Lahia area.

On Tuesday, 14-year-old Baraa was reported killed by tank fire in northern Nuseirat and in the early hours of this morning a shell hit a school where families are sheltering, injuring two children.

They are among eight children reported killed and 20 injured in just six days across the Gaza Strip, bringing the total number of children killed since the announcement of the October 2025 ceasefire to 351. This level of violence against children is unacceptable.

Children must be protected wherever they are. At home, while playing, walking to, or from, class, anywhere. They have suffered enough.

Gaza’s children are trying to recover their childhoods, to find some routine and stability in their young lives, which for too many have again been cut short. A ceasefire that does not protect children has failed them.

UNICEF calls on the Israeli authorities to take immediate and decisive action to protect children in line with their obligations under international humanitarian law. This includes respecting the principles of distinction, proportionality and precautions in all attacks, taking all feasible measures to avoid and minimize civilian harm, and ensuring that children receive the special protection to which they are entitled under international humanitarian law.

Authorities must also ensure transparent and robust accountability when children are killed or maimed and take effective action to deter further violence.”".

2,053 likes, 22 comments - unicef on October 31, 2026: "At a nutrition centre in Sudan, Samah gives her young daughter Sidra ready-to-use therapeutic food (RUTF), an energy-dense nutrient paste used to treat malnutrition.

Conflict, displacement, worsening food insecurity and economic hardships continue to drive a severe nutrition crisis across Sudan. 

UNICEF supports partners and nutrition centres like these, including in the hardest hit areas, to provide nutrition and health services to children and mothers.

What children in Sudan need the most is peace and access to the life-saving services they need.

© UNICEF/Elfatih".

2,144 likes, 20 comments - unicef on October 29, 2026: "1 billion.

That’s the number of doses of polio vaccines UNICEF procures and delivers around the world every year.

Ending polio and helping children survive and thrive means making sure they have access to vaccines and are protected against preventable diseases.

We have the knowledge and tools to #EndPolio forever. Now, more than ever, we must invest to realize every child’s right to health.

Link in bio to learn more.
#WorldPolioDay".

2,643 likes, 34 comments - unicef on October 29, 2026: "Afghanistan is one of two countries where wild polio continues to circulate.

Afifa, Mursal, Parasto and community mobilizers and vaccinators like them are on a mission to change that.

Through their determination, 12.7 million children have been vaccinated against the disease.

“Our work has not yet finished, our work still continues until we eradicate polio,” says Afifa.

#WordPolioDay".

1,676 likes, 18 comments - unicef on October 29, 2026: "Women spend 3.2 times more time on unpaid care than men. And, every day, girls aged 5–14 spend 160 million more hours on unpaid care and household chores than boys their age.
 
Care and support keep societies running. Yet this vital work too often falls to families alone, with women and girls shouldering a disproportionate share.

Paid parental leave, quality and affordable childcare, child benefits and inclusive social protection can help ease the burden, reduce gender inequalities and give children a better start in life.

UNICEF advocates for inclusive care and support systems that meet people’s needs at every age, recognise children as both caregivers and recipients of care, and provide decent work and social protection for care workers.

Ahead of 2028, the Year of Care and Support, UNICEF is calling for greater investment in care systems that leave no child, family or caregiver behind.

#DayOfCareAndSupport".

2,969 likes, 54 comments - unicef on October 29, 2026: "“This is not a ceasefire. This is a slow death,” says Nisreen, grandmother to three-year-old Rital in Gaza.

Rital was injured in an attack in July 2026 that also killed her mother and grandfather, while her father was killed earlier in the war.

Rital is still waiting for surgery related to the injuries she sustained.

Nisreen is doing everything to support Rital’s needs, but over a year since the ceasefire was announced in Gaza, childhood is still defined by survival. 

UNICEF is helping hundreds of thousands of children and families with health, nutrition, learning and psychosocial support services.

A ceasefire that does not protect children has failed them.

Children in Gaza must be protected as a priority.".

1,499 likes, 25 comments - unicef on October 28, 2026: "Recent escalations in Yemen have left about 110,000 children displaced.

Watch as 11-year-old Aisha, 8-year-old Mazen and 13-year-old Hamoud share their terrifying experiences, what they miss about their lives and what they hope for.

UNICEF is on the ground supporting children’s needs, but what they actually need is peace.".

1,257 likes, 13 comments - unicef on October 28, 2026: "In Chad, the lack of water and essential services in refugee camps puts children at risk of contracting polio.

Mamouna, a UNICEF-supported vaccinator, visits families and ensures their children receive life-saving immunization – bringing relief to mothers like Nannoya.

“If children are vaccinated, they won’t suffer from certain illnesses,” she says.

#WorldPolioDay".

2,244 likes, 23 comments - unicef on October 26, 2026: "Every Monday to Thursday, the Al-Hamidiyah health facility at a displacement camp in Sudan welcomes children and their parents.

Some have arrived on foot, others on trucks or donkeys – traveling from remote villages to ensure their children receive life-saving vaccines.

Behind this busy clinic is Ezzeldin, a vaccinator who has been protecting children’s health for over three decades. Now, even amid the ongoing conflict, he vaccinates more than 30 children a day.

From polio to measles, he makes sure children do not miss out on routine immunization because “diseases are like a war – they can destroy an entire generation”.

Leave a 💙 if Ezzeldin’s story inspired you!

#WorldPolioDay".
